National Special Security Events (NSSEs) and other contingency-driven special events. The objective is to establish multiple qualified sources that provide rapid access to local commercial vendors capable of supporting short-notice, high-visibility, and mission-essential event operations at government facilities and temporary event locations. This is a multiple-award, open-market BPA established under the authority of RFO 12.201-1(e)(3), using commercial-item simplified procedures, and acquired under RFO Part 12. 1.1 Background CES supports installation readiness, infrastructure sustainment, emergency response, and temporary facility requirements for planned and non-notice events. NSSE support often requires commercially available equipment and services that cannot be fully satisfied through organic inventory due to scale, timing, location, or mission-specific conditions. The BPA is intended to provide maximum flexibility for a wide range of temporary support requirements, including but not limited to power generation, climate control, sanitation, shelters, lighting, barriers, transportation-related rentals, emergency evacuation logistics support, and related event infrastructure. The 11th Wing requires flexibility to effectively sustain installation mission support activities.

Associated systems include: potable water, sewer, contaminated water reclamation and LCAC rinse facility, 400 Hz power provided to the apron and hangars, 100-foot apron lighting and compound security lighting, emergency diesel power generation, low pressure compressed air, fire detection and suppression prevention, physical security and cyber systems. As a tenant command on the Marine Corps Base, Camp Pendleton, ACU 5 must work with and through the base facilities organization to schedule and conduct repairs, upgrades and any new construction, while working through many other challenging processes such as environmental impact studies. Given the uniqueness of the LCAC and the fact most Sailors involved in maintenance come from ships and only serve one tour of duty in the LCAC community, they lack familiarity with the craft and its systems. The learning curve for personnel is steep and makes all tasks related to maintenance challenging and time consuming. In addition to complex maintenance, the LCAC requires in-depth cleaning to prevent corrosion on its aluminum hull and components. Even when not operating on the water, LCACs, by virtue of being located on the coast, are subject to severe corrosion due to salt and sand intrusion. Corrosion damage on LCACs is the number one driver of Non-Mission Capable (NMC) status at ACU5 and causes thousands of hours of costly weld repairs each year. Deep cleaning to remove salt and sand is necessary to keep the craft operational. 1.3. Objective: The goal of this effort is to improve the readiness and performance of LCACs at ACU 5.
